absent: Implementation and return conventions of the shared fixed-rate, gate, divider, mux and fixed-factor registration workers.
Definitions of external facilities such as SYM_START, BIT, container_of, spinlock primitives, clk_core, device objects, firmware nodes and debug filesystem entries.
Locking order, sleeping constraints and calling context for clock operation callbacks.
Validation of register field geometry, translation-table termination, parent index bounds and zero-divisor handling.
Producer-consumer memory ordering, wrap limits and concurrency rules for circular buffers beyond the masking formulas.
Meaning of core flag bits four and five and of any framework flags beyond those listed.
Generation, verification and enforcement of CFI type identifiers beyond publication of the stored value.

findings.text: SYM_TYPED_START forwards a symbol name with linkage and optional alignment to the generic symbol start facility. SYM_TYPED_FUNC_START builds on it by fixing linkage to global and alignment to the standard function alignment so callers supply only a name.

DEFINE_CFI_TYPE publishes a 32-bit read-only-after-init identifier for a function control-flow type. It forces the referenced function to be addressable so the compiler emits its type identifier, declares an external unsigned 32-bit object, and places a four-byte aligned global of that name in the read-only-after-init data section holding the compiler-generated identifier.

The circ_buf descriptor holds a pointer to byte storage plus two integer positions named head and tail. Head marks where producers insert and tail marks where consumers remove, with both advancing modulo the allocation size.

Occupancy and free-space helpers assume the buffer size is a power of two and use masking with one less than size. Occupancy is head minus tail under that mask. Free space reuses the same computation with tail and one past head swapped, which reserves one slot to distinguish full from empty.

To-end variants report the contiguous linear run available before wrapping. One computes occupancy limited to the distance from tail to the allocation end. The other computes free space limited to the distance from one past head to the end, accounting for the reserved slot, so callers can copy in at most two segments.
CLK_SET_RATE_GATE uses bit zero, CLK_SET_PARENT_GATE uses bit one, CLK_SET_RATE_PARENT uses bit two, and CLK_IGNORE_UNUSED uses bit three of the clock initialization flags.

CLK_GET_RATE_NOCACHE uses bit six, CLK_SET_RATE_NO_REPARENT uses bit seven, CLK_GET_ACCURACY_NOCACHE uses bit eight, CLK_RECALC_NEW_RATES uses bit nine, CLK_SET_RATE_UNGATE uses bit ten, CLK_IS_CRITICAL uses bit eleven, CLK_OPS_PARENT_ENABLE uses bit twelve, and CLK_DUTY_CYCLE_PARENT uses bit thirteen. Bits four and five are not defined by these fragments.

clk_rate_request carries negotiation state for one rate decision. It references the target core and states the desired rate with min_rate and max_rate bounds, then returns the selected best_parent_rate and best_parent_hw chosen during determination.

clk_duty expresses a ratio with num over den. clk_spread_spectrum groups modfreq_hz with spread_bp and a method selector. The clk_ssc_method enumeration maps CLK_SPREAD_NO, CLK_SPREAD_CENTER, CLK_SPREAD_UP and CLK_SPREAD_DOWN to the matching no, center, up and down spread constants.

Clock hardware operations expose a two-level power discipline. The prepare family with prepare, unprepare, is_prepared and unprepare_unused handles slow context setup, while the enable family with enable, disable, is_enabled and disable_unused handles fast gating. Context operations save_context and restore_context preserve state across low-power transitions.

Rate and topology operations separate query from commit. Recalculation helpers recalc_rate and recalc_accuracy derive current rate and accuracy from parent values, determine_rate selects a rate within a request, set_rate and set_rate_and_parent commit a rate with optional parent index change, and set_parent with get_parent switch and report the parent selector. A spread-spectrum setter set_spread_spectrum applies modulation configuration.

Signal-shaping and lifecycle operations complete the table. Phase accessors get_phase and set_phase exchange an angle in degrees, duty-cycle accessors get_duty_cycle and set_duty_cycle exchange a duty ratio structure, init and terminate bracket hardware use, and a debug hook debug_init receives a filesystem entry for provider-specific diagnostics.

clk_parent_data offers four alternative ways to identify a parent: a direct hardware handle hw, a firmware name fw_name, a plain name string name, or an integer index index. Callers populate the form available in their context.

clk_init_data describes a clock at registration with a name field, an operations table ops, a parent count num_parents, and general flags flags. Parent linkage is supplied in exactly one of three parallel arrays for names parent_names, parent-data records parent_data, or hardware handles parent_hws.
Registration requires that at most one of the three parent arrays in the init record is assigned. The count field must agree with the length of whichever array is chosen.
clk_hw links three references named core, clk and init, joining the internal core object to the consumer handle and the immutable registration record.
clk_fixed_rate embeds hw and adds fixed_rate, fixed_accuracy and flags for a constant-rate source.
CLK_FIXED_RATE_PARENT_ACCURACY uses bit zero of the fixed-rate flags to request accuracy inheritance from the parent.

The clk_hw_register_fixed_rate family wraps one internal worker with choices for lifetime, parent linkage and accuracy. Variants select managed versus unmanaged lifetime, identify the parent by name, hardware handle or parent-data record, and optionally supply an explicit accuracy or request parent-derived accuracy.

clk_gate models a single enable bit in a memory-mapped register. It embeds the generic hardware handle hw and records the register address reg, the bit position bit_idx within the register, a small flags field flags, and an optional lock pointer lock. A retrieval helper to_clk_gate derives the enclosing gate record from its hardware member.

CLK_GATE_SET_TO_DISABLE uses bit zero to invert enable polarity, CLK_GATE_HIWORD_MASK uses bit one to select masked-write access, and CLK_GATE_BIG_ENDIAN uses bit two to select big-endian register access.

The clk_hw_register_gate family forwards device, name, parent reference, general flags, register address, bit position, gate-specific flags and lock to shared workers. Family members vary managed versus unmanaged lifetime and parent lookup by name, hardware handle or parent-data record.

clk_div_table pairs a register value val with the divisor div it represents. clk_divider embeds the hardware handle hw and records a register address reg, field position and width named shift and width, a flags word flags, an optional translation table table, and an optional lock pointer lock. Helpers clk_div_mask and to_clk_divider compute a field mask from width and recover the enclosing divider from its hardware member.

Divider behavior flags assign bit zero to one-based encoding, bit one to power-of-two restriction, bit two to zero-value permission, bit three to masked-write access, bit four to closest rounding, bit five to read-only marking, bit six to maximum-at-zero encoding, bit seven to big-endian access, and bit eight to even-integer restriction. The corresponding constants are CLK_DIVIDER_ONE_BASED, CLK_DIVIDER_POWER_OF_TWO, CLK_DIVIDER_ALLOW_ZERO, CLK_DIVIDER_HIWORD_MASK, CLK_DIVIDER_ROUND_CLOSEST, CLK_DIVIDER_READ_ONLY, CLK_DIVIDER_MAX_AT_ZERO, CLK_DIVIDER_BIG_ENDIAN and CLK_DIVIDER_EVEN_INTEGERS.

The clk_hw_register_divider family shares workers that accept device, name, parent reference, general flags, register description, divider-specific flags, optional table and lock. Variants cover plain versus table-backed forms, managed versus unmanaged lifetime, and parent lookup by name, hardware handle or parent-data record, with a legacy alias defaulting to no table.

clk_mux models a parent selector field in a register. It embeds the hardware handle hw and records the register address reg, an optional value translation table table, a mask and shift named mask and shift, a small flags field flags and an optional lock pointer lock. A retrieval helper to_clk_mux recovers the enclosing mux from its hardware member.

Mux flags assign bit zero to one-based indexing, bit one to single-bit indexing, bit two to masked-write access, bit three to read-only marking, bit four to closest rounding, and bit five to big-endian access. The constants are CLK_MUX_INDEX_ONE, CLK_MUX_INDEX_BIT, CLK_MUX_HIWORD_MASK, CLK_MUX_READ_ONLY, CLK_MUX_ROUND_CLOSEST and CLK_MUX_BIG_ENDIAN.

The clk_hw_register_mux family forwards device, name, parent list with count, general flags, register field description, mux-specific flags, optional table and lock to shared workers. Variants differ in parent representation by names, hardware handles or parent-data records, in mask versus width field description, in table versus direct indexing, and in managed versus unmanaged lifetime, including a legacy alias that derives mask from width.

clk_fixed_factor scales a parent rate by integer ratio. It embeds the hardware handle hw and stores a multiplier mult, a divisor div, an accuracy value acc and a flags word flags. A retrieval helper to_clk_fixed_factor recovers the enclosing factor record from its hardware member.
CLK_FIXED_FACTOR_FIXED_ACCURACY uses bit zero of the fixed-factor flags to mark accuracy as fixed rather than derived.

The clk_hw_register_fixed_factor family wraps one worker with device, firmware node, name, parent reference, general flags, multiplier, divisor, accuracy, factor flags and lifetime selection. Variants choose parent by name, hardware handle or parent-data record and managed versus unmanaged lifetime.

Gate, divider and mux records each carry an optional spinlock pointer supplied at registration to serialize shared register updates. Callers that share a register provide a common lock, while private registers may pass no lock.

Clock control follows a staged lifecycle. Initialization init precedes use and termination terminate closes it. Slow preparation prepare must succeed before fast enabling enable, with query operations is_prepared and is_enabled reporting each stage and unused-cleanup operations unprepare_unused and disable_unused releasing resources left enabled by firmware. Context save_context and restore_context bracket suspend cycles.

Circular helpers evaluate their head, tail and size arguments more than once and require size to be a power of two with head and tail confined to integer range. Passing expressions with side effects, non-power-of-two sizes, or unsynchronized concurrent updates can yield incorrect counts or torn space reports.

Register-backed clocks assume caller-provided field geometry matches hardware. Incorrect shift, width, mask, bit position bit_idx, translation table table, or polarity and endianness flags can program reserved bits or select unintended parents and divisors. Read-only markings must be honored to avoid attempted writes to immutable fields.

Fixed-rate, gate, divider, mux and fixed-factor records all embed the generic hardware handle hw as their first member so the retrieval helpers to_clk_gate, to_clk_divider, to_clk_mux and to_clk_fixed_factor can convert from handle pointer to enclosing provider record.
Guards _LINUX_CIRC_BUF_H and __LINUX_CLK_PROVIDER_H make repeated inclusion idempotent. The former expands to one while the latter expands empty, but both prevent reprocessing.
